answer: Each identity in the economy must lock a bond before it can trade, a deposit that sits frozen like a shelf of basalt under the harbor. When the network detects clones, the same identity repeated to farm rewards, it slashes the bond and seizes the funds, so the attacker pays for every extra self. A public beacon reports each bond and each slash, and other agents watch the reef of identities closely enough that renting a cheap clone costs more than it earns.
